items.title: Central African Republic: ICC Verdict in Seleka Commander Case
items.description: Click to expand Image Mahamat Said Abdel Kani during closing statements in the courtroom of the International Criminal Court in The Hague, Netherlands, November 25, 2025. © 2025 ICC-CPi (The Hague) – The International Criminal Court (ICC)’s conviction of Mahamat Said Abdel Kani for crimes against humanity in the Central African Republic offers an important measure of long-awaited justice for victims of the abusive Seleka armed group, Human Rights Watch said today. In 2012, the predominantly Muslim Seleka rebels ousted the Central African Republic president, François Bozizé, and seized power through a campaign of violence and terror. In March 2013, the Seleka took control of Bangui, the capital, attacking civilians and pillaging the city. In late 2013, Christian and animist militias known as anti-balaka, began to organize counterattacks against the Seleka. Both the Seleka and anti-balaka have been implicated in widespread atrocities against civilians. “As the first ICC verdict against a high-level Seleka commander, the judgment against Said is a significant milestone in the fight against impunity for serious crimes in the Central African Republic,” said Lewis Mudge, Central Africa director at Human Rights Watch. “But this should only be considered a first step. The verdict is also a stark reminder of the ongoing abuses in the country, and the need for increased support for both international and domestic justice efforts to end the accountability gap that helps fuel recurring cycles of violence.” ICC judges convicted Said for crimes committed at the Central Office for the Repression of Banditry (Office Central de Répression du Banditisme, OCRB) in Bangui between April and August 2013. The crimes include imprisonment or other severe deprivation of physical liberty, torture, other inhumane acts, and persecution. Said was acquitted on the charges of war crimes. The majority of the judges found that the ouster of François Bozizé in March 2013 ended the conflict that had begun between the Seleka and the Central African armed forces in 2012, and therefore, there was no conflict at the time the alleged crimes were committed. Said was also acquitted for some incidents related to the crimes against humanity charges, including for lack of sufficient evidence. The court laid out a timeline for the sentencing proceedings, which will include a hearing in November. The court should take all necessary steps to ensure that affected communities in the Central African Republic learn about the judgment and next steps, including any appeals and reparations proceedings, Human Rights Watch said. Said is believed to have joined the Seleka in 2012 and was promoted to lieutenant, colonel, and then commander. In April 2013, when Seleka abuse in Bangui was acute, he was given a key role in the Central Office for the Repression of Banditry. The agency is a police unit created in the late 1990s to address a rise in banditry, which developed a reputation for abuse. Its abuse continues today and the government uses the unit at times to warn government critics of potential consequences of their criticism. Said was arrested in the Central African Republic and surrendered to the ICC on January 24, 2021. The court’s judges had issued an under-seal arrest warrant against him on January 7, 2019. In 2014, the Seleka splintered into several groups, including the Popular Front for the Renaissance (Front populaire pour la renaissance de la Centrafrique, FPRC), headed by Noureddine Adam and Michel Djotodia. Some factions of the FPRC aligned themselves with anti-balaka forces. Djotodia, who is sanctioned by the US Treasury, lives in Benin but returned to Bangui in 2020 for a short stay and is sometimes back in the country. Adam is reported to be between Chad and Sudan, where he continues to evade justice. On July 28, 2022, the ICC unsealed an arrest warrant against Adam, which was first issued against him under seal on January 7, 2019. ICC member countries should make every effort to support the court in arresting Adam and bring him to justice, Human Rights Watch said. Other high-profile Seleka leaders, such as Mahamat Al Khatim, Saleh Zabadi, and Ali Darassa, continue to lead splinter Seleka groups. In July 2025, ICC judges convicted two anti-balaka leaders, Alfred Yékatom and Patrice-Edouard Ngaïssona, for war crimes and crimes against humanity in the Central African Republic between December 2013 and August 2014. Yékatom and Ngaïssona were sentenced to 15 and 12 years in prison, respectively, and appeals are ongoing. Another anti-balaka commander, Maxim Mokom, was surrendered to the court in March 2022, but the prosecution withdrew the charges against him in October 2023, citing a lack of evidence and witnesses. The ICC opened the investigation into crimes committed in the Central African Republic since 2012, following a request from the Central African Republic government in 2014. This was the ICC’s second investigation into crimes committed in the country. The first investigation related to an earlier conflict, in 2002 and 2003, and resulted in the acquittal of Jean-Pierre Bemba, a former vice president from the Democratic Republic of Congo. In December 2022, the ICC prosecutor announced the completion of his office’s investigative activities in the Central African Republic. ICC investigations in the Central African Republic have been complemented by proceedings before the Special Criminal Court in Bangui, staffed by international and Central African judges and prosecutors. The court has issued verdicts in four cases and has several ongoing proceedings and investigations. This critical justice avenue is facing significant financial challenges. International partners should provide the court with the resources it needs to fulfill its important mandate, Human Rights Watch said. Said’s verdict comes at a time when the ICC is facing extreme pressure. In February 2025, US President Donald Trump issued an executive order authorizing sanctions on ICC officials and others supporting the court’s work. Since then, the US government has imposed sanctions on ICC officials and staff, a UN expert, and three leading Palestinian human rights organizations. Together with three other human rights groups, Human Rights Watch has sued the Trump administration in a US court over its sanctions targeting the ICC. On July 13, 2026, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced an escalated campaign to “dismantle” the court, including an increased use of sanctions and pressure on ICC member countries to leave the court. “The ICC is a critical court of last resort to deliver justice for the most serious crimes in the Central African Republic and across its docket,” Mudge said. “ICC member countries should redouble their efforts to protect the ICC and those supporting its work, so it can deliver on its essential global mandate.”

items.title: Près de 5 tonnes de volaille avariée saisies dans un abattoir de Mahdia
items.description: Lors d'une opération d'inspection menée ce mercredi les brigades de contrôle économique ont saisi 4,7 tonnes de poulets et de produits dérivés impropres à la consommation. La descente menée par mes services du gouvernorat en coordination avec l'Instance nationale de la sécurité sanitaire des produits alimentaires (INSSPA) a visé une entreprise de la région, spécialisée dans l'abattage de volailles et la distribution auprès des commerces locaux et a permis de révéler de multiples infractions graves. Selon un communiqué du gouvernorat, les contrôleurs ont notamment saisi des denrées périmées, notifié l'absence de mentions légales sur les dates de production, et un non-respect flagrant des conditions d'hygiène et de stockage. Outre les manquements sanitaires, les contrôleurs ont dressé un procès-verbal pour non-conformité des instruments de pesage et irrégularités sur la facturation. L'ensemble de la marchandise saisie sera détruit conformément aux procédures légales en vigueur, alors que l'enquête se poursuit, ajoute la même source. Y. N. L’article Près de 5 tonnes de volaille avariée saisies dans un abattoir de Mahdia est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Législatives 2026 : le PJD revendique la tête dans plusieurs circonscriptions clés
items.description: Au fur et à mesure que les procès-verbaux parviennent aux QG centraux des formations politiques après la fermeture des bureaux de vote ce mercredi 23 septembre 2026, le Parti de la Justice et de la Développement (PJD) affiche un premier optimisme. Selon les données préliminaires communiquées par la direction centrale de campagne de la lampe, le parti enregistrerait une avance significative dans plusieurs grandes circonscriptions électorales du Royaume. S'exprimant au nom de la direction électorale du parti, Abdelali Hamieddine a affirmé que les premiers dépouillements placent le PJD en tête dans un nombre important de bureaux de vote. Le dirigeant politique a fait état d'un écart notable avec ses concurrents directs, soutenant qu'aucune formation n'émerge à ce stade comme un poursuivant immédiat, les voix restant dispersées entre les autres acteurs en lice. Interrogé sur la cartographie de ces premières tendances, le représentant du PJD a cité plusieurs grands centres urbains et fiefs électoraux, notamment Rabat, Temara, Casablanca, Fès, Meknès, Tanger, Agadir, Inezgane, Taroudant et Sidi Slimane. Ces déclarations interviennent alors que le décompte officiel des bulletins se poursuit sous la supervision des autorités administratives compétentes pour établir les résultats définitifs du scrutin. items.title: ZAC Mbao : un homme interpellé après plusieurs vols de scooters sous couvert d’essais
items.description: Le Commissariat d’arrondissement de ZAC Mbao a interpellé, le 23 septembre 2026, un individu soupçonné d’escroquerie et de vol portant sur plusieurs scooters. Son arrestation fait suite à une plainte déposée le 1er septembre contre X. Les investigations techniques menées par les enquêteurs ont permis de localiser le suspect au niveau du rond-point Sedima, où il a été interpellé. Entendu sur procès-verbal, le premier plaignant a expliqué avoir publié en ligne une annonce pour la vente de son scooter Yamaha X-Max, proposé à 900 000 francs CFA. Contacté par le mis en cause, il avait fixé un rendez-vous au rond-point de la ZAC Mbao. Sur place, le prétendu acheteur a demandé à essayer le deux-roues avant de finaliser la transaction. Une fois les clés en main, il a pris la fuite avec le scooter et a cessé tout contact avec le propriétaire. La poursuite des investigations a permis d'établir que le suspect serait également impliqué dans deux autres affaires similaires. Une deuxième victime, contactée par les enquêteurs, s’est présentée au commissariat et l’a formellement identifié lors d’une confrontation. Elle a déclaré avoir publié une annonce pour la vente de son scooter Beverly avant d’être contactée, le 20 septembre, par le même individu. Celui-ci aurait utilisé le même procédé, en demandant à essayer le véhicule avant de prendre la fuite. Une troisième victime s’est ensuite présentée spontanément au service. Elle a relaté des faits similaires survenus le 19 septembre vers 12 heures devant le magasin Auchan de Grand Mbao, concernant également un scooter Beverly. Interrogé sur ces différentes affaires, le mis en cause a partiellement reconnu les faits, admettant uniquement ceux dénoncés par le premier plaignant. Il a déclaré avoir revendu le Yamaha X-Max pour 500 000 francs CFA à un individu rencontré à Keur Massar. Lors de son interpellation, les enquêteurs ont également découvert en sa possession 1 455 100 francs CFA. Interrogé sur la provenance de cette somme, il a évoqué une activité de vente de véhicules, sans présenter de justificatif. L’argent a été saisi et placé sous scellé. Les investigations se poursuivent afin de retrouver les scooters dérobés, d’identifier d’éventuels receleurs, de déterminer l’origine des fonds saisis et de vérifier l’existence d’autres victimes.

items.title: At UNGA 81: Nigeria, Italy join forces in massive $5bn global education funding
items.description: —Vision aligns with our agenda to improve outcomes, invest in access, capacity building- Tinubu—Education driving Nigeria’s economic future, prosperity, says VP Shettima By Johnbosco Agbakwuru Nigeria and Italy on Wednesday strengthened collaboration to implement the proposed Global Partnership for Education (GPE) financing campaign targeted at mobilizing $5 billion for education financing worldwide. This is just as President Bola Tinubu has said the GPE vision aligns with Nigeria’s agenda which aims at improving educational outcomes by investing in access as well as capacity building for teachers. President Tinubu stated this in New York, United States, during the Multiply Possibility High-level event tagged, “A New Era for Education Financing” held on the margins of the ongoing 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly. In his intervention, President Tinubu, in a video message, also commended stakeholders in the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) for their efforts in accelerating education financing globally. Speaking at the event, the Vice President, Senator Kashim Shettima, who is representing the Nigerian President at the global gathering, noted that education is an investment in Nigeria’s economic future, and productivity as well as the prosperity and stability of its citizens, stressing that it is not merely an expenses at the margins of the country’s development agenda. “For Nigeria, education is not an expenditure at the margins of our development agenda. It is an investment in our economic future, national productivity, and the prosperity and stability of our people. “Since President Bola Ahmed Tinubu assumed office in 2023, our Administration has substantially increased resources devoted to education, while pursuing reforms to strengthen basic education financing, expand foundational learning, and improve access to tertiary and technical education. “Through the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, we are widening access to higher education, while strengthening the link between education, skills, employment and enterprise.” According to VP Shettima, while Nigeria is also looking beyond traditional budgetary allocations, President Tinubu has directed that liquid funds recovered by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, once legally cleared and free from litigation, be channelled to the Nigerian Education Loan Fund. To carry out the President’s directive, he said the Federal Executive Council (FEC) recently approved consideration of unclaimed dividends and dormant funds for the same purpose, subject to the relevant legal requirements. This, Senator Shettima explained, demonstrates the nation’s conviction that financing education needs mobilisation of every responsible and lawful domestic source available. Citing Nigeria’s alliances with the World Bank and GPE through HOPE-EDU, the Nigerian Vice President underscored what international partnership could achieve, just as he said, “The programme is expected to reach approximately 29 million children and 500,000 teachers across Nigeria.” He continued: “This is precisely why GPE matters. GPE does not replace national investment; it multiplies it. The ambition before us is to mobilise US$5 billion for GPE and, through that investment, unlock additional financing for education in partner countries. ‘Domestic resources must remain the anchor, complemented by development assistance, concessional finance, philanthropy and innovative financing.” Senator Shettima further observed that although Nigeria is a young country whose growing population could become one of its greatest economic assets, adding that this is possible only if the nation’s “young people have access to quality education, relevant skills and meaningful opportunities.” The answer to declining global aid, he pointed out, “must therefore be smarter multilateralism: using scarce international resources to leverage much larger investments.” He urged participants at the high-level event to ensure that it is not merely a fundraising exercise, “but a renewed compact for human capital, bringing together national leadership, international partnership and responsible financing so that every child has the opportunity to learn, thrive and contribute to their country’s future.” Expressing Nigeria’s appreciation to the Italian government and GPE for joining in the conversation on the future of education financing, VP Shettima said as co-hosts of the campaign, Nigeria is not participating merely to ask the international community to invest more in education but “to demonstrate that we are investing in education ourselves.” Earlier in a video presentation, the Prime Minister of Italy, HE Giorgia Meloni, praised President Tinubu’s leadership and Nigeria’s determination to improve educational outcomes across all levels. He urged all partners in the global alliance to show greater commitment to reversing the trend in developing countries. For her part, UN Deputy Secretary General, Dr Amina Mohammed, thanked all partners for the interest shown in the improvement of education financing in developing countries, noting that the changes sought by stakeholders should begin with the choices that governments make. She called on International Finance Institutions to support committed countries in finding the fiscal spaces needed to improve educational outcomes, including capacity building for teachers whose motivation and training remain critical to achieving set objectives. In the same vein, Chair of Board of Directors of GPE, Dr. Jakaya Kikwete, underscored the need for accelerating education financing, noting that the event was a reminder to the fact that education remained central to the attainment of human rights, security, and peace, among other benefits. He stated that GPE is driven by the realities of the drop in development assistance in education amidst the widening financing gap and the fact that the world will increasingly depend on systems that deliver tangible and desirable outcomes For her part, girls’ education activist, Malala Yousafzai, emphasised the need for collaboration in ideas and resources, stating that global partnerships tend to produce greater results and more impactful outcomes than isolated interventions by countries. She urged all stakeholders, especially multilateral organisations and governments across the world, to commit more resources and efforts to gender equality in education and address specific needs of the girl child, especially in developing countries. Governments and donors at the high-level event made generous contributions towards the education of at least 370 million children globally, with the government of Italy pledging the sum of 50 million Euros for GPE programmes and Interventions. “I don’t see any rational basis” – Inusah Fuseini rejects proposed five-year term
items.description: Former Tamale Central MP Inusah Fuseini has rejected the proposal to extend the tenure of the President and Members of Parliament from four to five years. The proposal is contained in the report of the Constitution Review Committee chaired by Professor H. Kwasi Prempeh. The government has accepted the recommendation, arguing that an additional year would give governments more time to formulate, implement and assess policies. However, speaking at a press briefing on Wednesday, September 23, ahead of an Institute of Economic Affairs (IEA) seminar on the constitutional review, Mr Fuseini questioned the rationale for extending the tenure. He argued that the current four-year term already provides sufficient time for an elected government to implement its policies. “And if you are running four years, the last year is used for campaigning for re-election. Probably you can have three years if you have been re-elected a second time. “So why do you say five? If the argument is that you have the first year to set up your government and the last year to run a campaign, what is the rationale for five? Because from that argument, you see that two years have been lost. So why five? I don’t see any rational basis for five,” he said. Mr Fuseini also rejected the argument that a five-year term would improve policy continuity. According to him, the 1992 Constitution already provides for continuity in governance through the Directive Principles of State Policy. “Talk about continuity. The Constitution already anticipated that. That is why in the Directive Principles of State Policy, every succeeding President must, as far as possible, continue with ongoing projects,” he said. He argued that the constitutional arrangement recognises that a President may not be able to complete all policy initiatives within a single term and that subsequent governments can continue or improve on existing projects. “So the Constitution anticipated that a President might not be able to exhaust all his policy options and the government may improve the projects that it has undertaken. And I think the constitutional arrangement must be respected,” he added. The former MP was speaking ahead of the IEA’s “Views and Reflections” seminar on the Prempeh Committee’s report and the government’s position on proposed constitutional reforms. The IEA itself has rejected the proposed extension of presidential and parliamentary terms, arguing that four years is sufficient for an elected government to implement its programme

items.title: Constitution shouldn’t be amended simply because years have passed – IEA
items.description: The Institute of Economic Affairs (IEA) has cautioned against amending Ghana’s Constitution merely because a certain number of years have elapsed. The Institute said that while there are merits to the arguments on both sides of the constitutional review debate, there should be a continuous assessment of how the Constitution is functioning. According to the IEA representative, such continuous examination does not necessarily mean that amendments must be made at fixed intervals. “We should continuously examine how the Constitution is functioning. But that does not mean the Constitution must be amended simply because a particular number of years have passed. Constitutional maintenance should be continuous, even if constitutional amendments are occasional.” The comments come amid ongoing discussions over the process of reviewing Ghana’s 1992 Constitution and proposals for reforms to address identified gaps in the country’s governance framework. The IEA maintained that the focus should be on ensuring that the Constitution continues to function effectively, rather than treating the passage of time as an automatic basis for amendment.

items.title: L’Initiative pour la gouvernance mondiale propulse le Sud global vers la modernité (Par Mamadou Yaya Diallo)
items.description: BEIJING, 21 septembre (Xinhua) — En septembre 2026, l'Initiative pour la gouvernance mondiale (IGM) célèbre son premier anniversaire. Cette année aura été celle où le Sud global a pris l'initiative de façonner un nouvel ordre et une nouvelle structure internationale. Le Sénégal et la Chine ont activement renforcé leur dialogue et leur coopération multilatéraux : en décembre 2025, le Sénégal est devenu membre fondateur du Groupe des amis de la gouvernance mondiale; en juillet 2026, il est devenu membre fondateur de l'Organisation mondiale de coopération en matière d'intelligence artificielle (IA). Ces deux cartes de « membre fondateur » illustrent parfaitement que les pays du Sud global s'unissent et coopèrent pour faire progresser leur modernisation respective, relever les défis mondiaux et pratiquer un véritable multilatéralisme. PROMOUVOIR L'EGALITE DE GOUVERNANCE, CONSOLIDER LE SOCLE DE LA SOUVERAINETE Parmi les cinq concepts fondamentaux de l'IGM – l'égalité souveraine, l'état de droit international, le multilatéralisme, l'approche centrée sur l'humain et l'orientation vers l'action – c'est l'égalité souveraine qui occupe la première place. Depuis longtemps, la répartition des droits de vote au sein des institutions financières internationales, le partage des responsabilités de réduction des émissions dans les négociations climatiques, et la rédaction des règles de gouvernance de l'IA sont souvent dominés par quelques pays développés. Les pays africains représentent près d'un tiers des Etats membres de l'ONU, mais demeurent « la majorité silencieuse » sur de nombreux enjeux cruciaux. La création du Groupe des amis de la gouvernance mondiale a bâti une plateforme inclusive pour réformer et améliorer le système de gouvernance mondiale, rassemblant la sagesse collective et mobilisant les efforts communs. REUNIR LA FORCE DU SUD GLOBAL, BATIR LE PONT DE LA COOPERATION Le Forum sur la coopération sino-africaine (FCSA) constitue le pont clé qui traduit les concepts en action. Lors du Sommet de Beijing en 2024, le président Xi Jinping a avancé les six propositions pour faire progresser conjointement la modernisation sino-africaine, et annoncé les dix actions de partenariat pour la modernisation à mener avec l'Afrique au cours des trois prochaines années. Des routes aux ports, du commerce électronique transfrontalier à la coopération spatiale, la coopération sino-africaine traduit l'esprit de sincérité, de résultats réels, d'amitié et de bonne foi en résultats tangibles pour le développement partagé. Carrefour en Afrique de l'Ouest et membre important de l'Union africaine, le Sénégal s'engage pleinement sur cette dynamique de coopération. L'exonération tarifaire totale, les équipes médicales mobiles, les préparatifs des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse… Chaque avancée dans la coopération accélérée entre la Chine et le Sénégal est une illustration de l'IGM qui prend racine en Afrique. PRENDRE DE L'AVANCE SUR L'IA, OUVRIR LA VOIE VERS L'AVENIR En juillet 2026, le ministre sénégalais des Télécommunications et du Numérique, M. Samba Diouf, s'est rendu à Shanghai pour assister à la cérémonie de signature de l'Accord portant sur la création de l'Organisation mondiale de coopération en matière d'IA, et a signé l'accord au nom du gouvernement du Sénégal, faisant ainsi du Sénégal l'un des 29 Etats membres fondateurs de l'organisation. La portée profonde de cet accord réside dans ce qui suit : alors que les pays occidentaux tentent de « restreindre à un petit cercle » les règles de gouvernance de l'IA, les pays du Sud global s'unissent pour ramener la gouvernance de l'IA sous le cadre multilatéral des Nations Unies, adhérant au principe d'une approche centrée sur l'humain et orientée vers le progrès et le bien, en faisant de l'IA une grande force motrice de la prospérité partagée et de la sécurité commune. Face à la question d'époque « au service de qui la gouvernance mondiale? » , la réponse de l'IGM est claire et ferme : au service du Sud global, des pays en développement, et des peuples du monde entier. Fort de son double statut de membre fondateur, le Sénégal est prêt à travailler avec la Chine et les autres pays du Sud global pour tirer pleinement parti de l'économie numérique et construire ensemble un ordre international juste et équitable, afin que la lumière de la modernisation illumine chaque pouce de terre du Sud global. Fin Mamadou Yaya Diallo est professeur de droit international à l'Université Cheikh Anta Diop de Dakar. Les opinions exprimées dans cet article sont celles de l'auteur et ne reflètent pas nécessairement les positions de l'Agence de presse Xinhua.

items.title: Tinubu’s ‘working vacation argument’ illiterate – Odinkalu
items.description: By Dickson Omobola Former Chairman of the National Human Rights Commission, NHRC, Professor Chidi Odinkalu, has criticised the Presidency’s description of President Bola Tinubu’s absence from the country as a working vacation, saying the argument is being pushed by illiterates. Odinkalu also lamented that while the world was discussing education at the United Nations General Assembly, UNGA, the Tinubu administration had no education policy. Speaking on Politics Today, a Channels Television programme, he said the number of out-of-school children was skyrocketing in the country, while there was no visible education policy to present to the world. He said: “The world is discussing education. At the moment, as you probably know, there is a crisis with unity schools in Nigeria over the concessioning of King’s College. There is no policy on the concessioning of publicly owned schools, by the way, so this is just drawn out of the heart. Actually, the current administration does not have an education policy. The last education policy was developed by Adamu Adamu as Minister of Education in 2017, and I don’t even think this administration has read it. They have not bothered to update it. “The number of out-of-school children is skyrocketing in the country, and we can’t even go to the United Nations and say, ‘This is our education policy.’ That’s how bad it is. And suddenly, the President does not have a calling card on this because he cannot name any teacher who taught him, and he cannot name the schools he attended. Do you see the credibility crisis we are facing by attending an education summit at the United Nations General Assembly?” On the absence of the President and his vice from the country, he said: “This is the first administration where the vice president and the president are making a habit of abandoning the country without leadership. It never happened before. As a rule, as a convention, pretty much a binding convention of government, no president allowed himself to be out of the country with the vice president at the same time. It never happened. “It was not permitted. This is the first time that it has become a habit. Under the late Muhammadu Buhari, whenever Buhari was going out of the country, Osinbajo was required to be back in the country. Under Obasanjo, Obasanjo would never contemplate it. Yar’Adua did not contemplate it. Jonathan did not allow it. “No matter how you read the text of Section 145, the idea of a working vacation does not exist in that text. What Section 145 addresses is absence from the country for a duration set at 21 days. Irrespective of whether the President transmits a transfer of authority enabling the Vice President to act, upon the onset of the 21st day, something should happen. “Now, the only thing is that, if you are being overly technical, and I were counsel to the Presidency, I would not be talking about this idea of a working vacation or a non-working vacation. That sounds quite illiterate, with the greatest, most profound respect. If I were counsel to the Presidency, what I would do, to sound very overly legalistic about this, is to use the Interpretation Act and say that 21 days means 21 working days. At the moment, that is not yet the case.” Vanguard News The post Tinubu’s ‘working vacation argument’ illiterate – Odinkalu appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: JOJ 2026 : Dakar fait le ménage dans son espace public
items.description: Dans la nuit du 21 septembre, un important dispositif a été déployé par le ministère de l’Intérieur et de la Sécurité publique dans le cadre d’une vaste opération de désencombrement et de sécurisation dans la région de Dakar. Cette initiative a mobilisé conjointement les forces de défense et de sécurité en prélude aux Jeux Olympiques de la jeunesse (Joj), « Dakar 2026 ». Au rond-point de la Place Washington, une compagnie de policiers au garde-à-vous salue le ministre de l'Intérieur, Mouhamadou Makhtar Cissé. Après les salutations d’usage, les policiers reposent leurs mains droites, posées un instant plus tôt sur leurs bérets rouges, et claquent des cuisses à l'unisson pour marquer le top départ officiel de cette soirée de désencombrement dans la région de Dakar. D'un pas dynamique, le ministre se dirige vers la première étape de l’opération : Dakar-Plateau. Il est presque 21 heures. Des chariots élévateurs, des chargeuses-pelleteuses et des camions suivent le cortège avant de prendre possession des lieux quelques minutes plus tard. Sous la lumière blanche des lampadaires, une chargeuse-pelleteuse occupée par trois hommes commence à détruire les panneaux publicitaires. Les bruits de choc résonnent lourdement dans l'air, saturé par les émanations d'échappement des engins. Au rythme des impacts, deux panneaux s'écroulent de tout leur poids. Un troisième, plus résistant, encaisse les coups pendant près de cinq minutes avant de céder à son tour. L'ensemble des opérations se déroule sous le regard vigilant des agents de la Ville de Dakar, de la commune de Dakar-Plateau et des services du cadre de vie. Puis, les équipes commencent à enlever les voitures en stationnement, qu'elles soient en bon état ou en panne. Soulevées par un charriot élévateur, telles Simba brandi par Rafiki, elles sont déposées une à une, avec précaution, sur les porte-engins. Aux premières loges de ce spectacle, Alioune Ndoye, maire de Dakar-Plateau, salue cette opération de désencombrement. Il affirme que la région de Dakar avait besoin d'une telle initiative « pour retrouver son cadre de vie, surtout en prélude aux Joj “Dakar 2026“ ». Ici, la sécurité demeure la priorité absolue, et les consignes de prudence ainsi que les appels à la vigilance fusent de toutes parts. Après Dakar-Plateau, le cortège met le cap sur Rebeuss. Il est plus de 22 heures lorsque les fresques murales de la maison d'arrêt accueillent le convoi. Installations illégales Les véhicules garés entre le Palais de justice et la prison ne sont pas épargnés : ils sont embarqués à leur tour. L'opération de désencombrement prend alors un nouvel élan, et la longue file de véhicules s'ébranle désormais en direction des Parcelles Assainies. Le convoi arrive ensuite au rond-point « Case-Ba », sur l'axe menant à Cambérène. Sur place, les forces de police sont déployées en nombre face à une foule partagée entre partisans et opposants à l'opération. Sous le regard contrasté des habitants, le ministre de l'Intérieur a tenu à rassurer : l’État œuvre pour le bien de tous et non l’inverse. Vêtu d’un ensemble traditionnel bleu, il a rappelé aux occupants de la zone qu’il était impératif de remettre de l’ordre dans cet espace public, qui représente parfois une menace sécuritaire. Selon lui, le cycle perpétuel de la réoccupation illégale des voies publiques doit cesser. Il a assuré que, cette fois, l’État prendrait toutes les dispositions nécessaires pour garantir un suivi rigoureux. « Après ces démantèlements et ces enlèvements, une présence policière sera déployée sur les lieux pour assurer le suivi, mais aussi pour garantir la sécurité », a-t-il déclaré. Djamil Sané, maire des Parcelles Assainies venu assister aux opérations lancées par le ministre de l’Intérieur, estime qu’il est urgent de rétablir l'ordre dans la zone. Il confie que ces deux voies abritent un marché informel où sévissent des receleurs qui alimentent l'insécurité. Un collectif regroupant les riverains des Unités 6, 7 et 8 s’était d’ailleurs rendu à son bureau pour dénoncer ces violences et ces désagréments. Pendant ce temps, les engins poursuivaient leur travail dans un vacarme assourdissant, tandis que les équipes de la Sonaged profitaient de la nuit pour nettoyer et dégager les lieux. Au rond-point de Bountou Pikine, le ministre Mouhamadou Makhtar Cissé et le maire Abdoulaye Timbo ont supervisé l’opération de désencombrement visant à démolir les installations illégales (toitures en zinc, panneaux publicitaires) et à nettoyer la voie publique avec le concours de la Sonaged. Cette initiative s'inscrit dans le cadre de la sécurisation de la région de Dakar, de l'amélioration du cadre de vie et des préparatifs pour les Joj. Tout en rappelant que le désencombrement relève d'abord des collectivités territoriales, le ministre a affirmé le soutien de l'État et appelé à une coordination rigoureuse pour éviter tout désordre institutionnel. Sur le terrain, l'opération suscite l'adhésion des autorités, tandis que des artisans impactés, bien que touchés par la destruction de leurs aménagements, reconnaissent le bien-fondé de cette lutte contre l'occupation anarchique. Lamine SARR & Aziz Méthiour NDIAYE (Stagiaires)

items.title: Access Bank, Visa launch ‘Visa Accept’ in Ghana
items.description: Visa, a global leader in digital payments, in partnership with Access Bank (Ghana) Plc., today unveiled Visa Accept , a solution that allows micro, nano and small merchants across Ghana to accept contactless card payments directly on their smartphones, without the need for additional hardware. Visa Accept helps to address a key challenge facing many of Ghana’s smallest businesses. While digital payment adoption continues to grow across the country, many micro and nano merchants have remained excluded from card acceptance due to the cost and complexity of traditional point-of-sale (POS) infrastructure. Through Visa Accept, merchants can create a seller profile within the Access Bank mobile banking app and begin accepting payments within minutes. Consumers can pay using a contactless card or mobile wallet, scan a QR code, or receive a secure payment link, eliminating the need for dedicated POS hardware. Funds are settled to the merchant’s existing bank account in near real-time, while transactions benefit from Visa’s security standards and consumer protections, including support for disputes and refunds. ” Consumer demand for digital payments in Ghana continues to grow, but acceptance among smaller merchants continues to face challenges. Visa Accept is helping close that gap by making it easier and more affordable for micro and small businesses to accept digital payments using the smartphones they already own. By expanding access to digital acceptance, we are helping more merchants participate in the digital economy while providing consumers with more ways to pay easily and securely.” said Fabrice Konan, Country Manager, Visa Ghana. Also speaking on the launch, Eugene Ocansey, Executive Director, Retail and SME Banking, Access Bank (Ghana) Plc, said “Access Bank is proud to be the first bank in Ghana to partner Visa on this solution. The bulk of businesses in our country are SMEs, and Visa Accept gives us an opportunity to start transitioning those who are informal into the formal economy. When a merchant has a tool that brings in their money and makes their cash flow visible, we can understand what the business does, and that is what makes the average SME bankable. Visa brings the technology; Access Bank brings the reach to put it in the hands of every merchant who needs it.” Visa Accept is now available to eligible Access Bank Ghana customers nationwide. Merchants can enroll through the Access Bank mobile banking app or visit an Access Bank branch for assistance.

items.title: Sebta : Sanchez salue les mesures prises par le Maroc après de nouveaux appels à franchir la frontière
items.description: Le Premier ministre, espagnol Pedro Sánchez a salué mercredi les mesures prises par le Maroc pour renforcer son dispositif à la frontière avec Sebta, au lendemain de nouveaux appels lancés sur les réseaux sociaux pour gagner cette enclave espagnole située en Afrique du Nord. « Hier, nous avons vu un déploiement très important de forces de police (marocaines), aussi bien à la frontière de Sebta qu'à la frontière de Melilla, à la suite d'alertes apparues sur les réseaux sociaux », a rapporté le dirigeant socialiste lors d'une conférence de presse en marge de l'Assemblée générale de l'ONU à New York. « Il faut le reconnaître », a-t-il admis, quelques heures après un entretien avec le maire de gauche de New York, Zohran Mamdani. Mardi, le Premier ministre espagnol avait imputé dans un entretien à CNN la récente crise migratoire survenue à Sebta à un échec des contrôles frontaliers marocains. S'exprimant devant le Parlement le 3 septembre, le chef du gouvernement espagnol avait tenu à souligner qu'il n'existait aucune « preuve solide » indiquant que le Maroc avait orchestré cet événement. Sur le plan intérieur, Pedro Sánchez a été vivement accueilli par l'opposition de droite et d'extrême droite pour une soi-disant clémence envers Rabat après ces événements inédits, qui ont également provoqué une crise diplomatique au sein de l'Union européenne. Les 30 et 31 juillet, plus de 70.000 migrants sont entrés à Sebta, à la nage ou à pied depuis le Maroc, lors d'un afflux massif au cours duquel plusieurs dizaines d'entre eux sont décédés, principalement en mer, d'après les autorités à Madrid et Rabat. Depuis, la plupart de ces migrants sont retournés au Maroc. Toutefois, plusieurs milliers de personnes demeurent dans l'enclave, où la situation s'est depuis dégradée. The post Sebta : Sanchez salue les mesures prises par le Maroc après de nouveaux appels à franchir la frontière appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Burkina : Les députés adoptent à l'unanimité la loi de finances rectificative pour l'exécution du budget de l'État, exercice 2026
items.description: L'Assemblée législative du peuple (ALP) a, à l'unanimité de ses membres, adopté ce mercredi 23 septembre 2026 le projet de loi portant loi de finances rectificative de la loi de finances pour l'exécution du budget de l'État, exercice 2026. Cette loi se caractérise par une ouverture de 301 milliards de FCFA de recettes supplémentaires qui seront affectées notamment à des dépenses d'investissements structurants, fait ressortir le ministre de l'économie et des finances, Dr Aboubakar Nacanabo, entouré de ses proches collaborateurs, dont la ministre déléguée chargée du budget, Fatoumata Bako. À l'issue de l'adoption à l'unanimité des 71 députés de l'Assemblée législative du peuple (ALP), le ministre de l'économie et des finances, Dr Aboubakar Nacanabo, est revenu sur le contexte qui a prévalu à la démarche. « En début d'année, nous avons commencé l'exécution du budget de l'exercice 2026, sur la base du vote qui a été fait par l'ALP. La loi prévoit qu'en cours d'exécution, s'il y a des évènements qui nécessitent que nous puissions revenir vers l'Assemblée pour voter une loi de finances rectificative, nous puissions le faire. Effectivement, nous avons donc fait le suivi de l'exécution du budget et le rapport à mi-parcours a montré que l'exécution se passait très bien, avec le recouvrement des recettes qui dépasse largement ce que nous avions prévu et l'exécution des dépenses qui se passe très bien. Donc, dans un tel contexte, il est important que nous puissions engager des travaux pour une loi des finances rectificative, afin de prendre en charge les recettes supplémentaires qui ont été recouvrées ou qui sont prévues pour être recouvrées d'ici la fin de l'année. C'est cela qui nous a amenés à proposer cette loi de finances rectificative à l'Assemblée », situe le ministre, signifiant que l'augmentation de recettes donne donc la possibilité d'ouvrir de nouvelles dépenses qui vont être prises en charge par ces nouvelles recettes. Le ministre Aboubakar Nacanabo et Mme la ministre déléguée chargée du budget, Fatoumata Bako, suivant attentivement l'examen du projet de loi dans l'hémicycle. Lire aussi : Budget 2026 : Les dépenses révisées à la hausse d'environ 297 milliards de FCFA « Pour notre loi de finances rectificative, nous avons fait une ouverture de 301 milliards de recettes supplémentaires, qui viennent s'ajouter à ce qui avait été prévu initialement. Et ces 301 milliards, il fallait maintenant voir comment les affecter à des dépenses, notamment des dépenses d'investissement structurantes. Il faut dire qu'à l'issue de cette loi de finances rectificative, il ressort une amélioration de ce qu'on appelle l'épargne budgétaire. L'épargne budgétaire, c'est ce qui reste quand on couvre les dépenses de fonctionnement par les recettes ordinaires. Cela veut dire que nos recettes ordinaires (c'est-à-dire les recettes fiscales et non fiscales), si on les utilise pour réaliser les dépenses ordinaires (dépenses de fonctionnement et de transferts), il ressort plus de 900 milliards, soit une hausse de près de 35 % par rapport à ce qui était prévu initialement. Ce qui nous donne une marge pour réaliser des investissements structurants. C'est dans ce sens que des investissements importants ont été ouverts, notamment en termes d'infrastructures (infrastructures immobilières, routières…), d'équipements (acquisitions de véhicules automobiles au profit du parc de l'État). Il y a également des investissements importants comme le projet Bangr-wéogo qui est en cours, des investissements comme la phase II du projet SMART (projet qui nous permet à travers les caméras de pouvoir surveiller la ville, surveiller la circulation et de faire ce qu'on a appelé l'e-verbalisation) », a présenté le ministre de l'économie et des finances, Dr Aboubakar Nacanabo. A l'issue de l'adoption, le ministre Nacanabo a félicité également les députés et l'ensemble de tous ceux qui ont travaillé à rendre effective la loi. Lire aussi : Burkina/Budget 2026 : L'épargne budgétaire progresse de 35,59% dans la loi de finances rectificative Selon l'autorité, il importe de toujours regarder comment renforcer davantage les recouvrements de recettes, en ce sens que les besoins de développement du Burkina sont très importants et le gouvernement est animé de grandes ambitions. « Nous pouvons être satisfaits de ce qui est réalisé, mais nous avons toujours le devoir de pouvoir toujours faire plus, pour faire face donc aux nombreux besoins qui sont les nôtres », a-t-il affirmé, appuyant que ce projet de loi de finances rectificative va permettre de renforcer les investissements prévus dans le cadre du plan RELANCE . Le ministre Nacanabo a saisi l'instant pour féliciter notamment les régies de recettes pour les bonnes performances qui ont été réalisées, les contribuables pour leur civisme fiscal et « inviter tous les ordonnateurs de budget à exécuter efficacement les dépenses, à faire en sorte que chaque franc investi puisse contribuer à transformer qualitativement la vie des Burkinabè ». Lire aussi : Burkina : Plus de 107% de recouvrement des recettes au premier trimestre 2026 O.L Lefaso.net

items.title: ‘Our young people must inherit story of what Africa created, not lost’ – Mahama
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has called for the restoration of Africa’s cultural heritage to help future generations reconnect with the continent’s history, achievements and identity. He said young Africans should not inherit only the narrative of what the continent lost through conquest, colonialism and the removal of its cultural treasures, but should also have access to evidence of what African societies created and achieved. Speaking at a High-Level Side Event on the Next Steps on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York, President Mahama said the return of African artefacts was important to how young people understand their history. “Our young people must inherit more than the story of what Africa lost. They must inherit the story of what Africa created,” he said. He said the presence of African artefacts on the continent would allow future generations to directly engage with tangible evidence of their ancestors’ achievements. According to President Mahama, a young African visiting a museum on the continent should be able to see evidence that Africa’s history did not begin with subjugation. “She learns that her history did not begin with subjugation. She learns that her ancestors built empires, mastered metallurgy, engineered complex political systems, and created sublime art.” He said the restitution of cultural heritage was therefore not simply about returning physical objects but about restoring connections between African communities, their history and their identity. President Mahama said Ghana’s campaign for reparatory justice was focused on building partnerships to address the consequences of historical injustices. “Ghana does not come to this hall to assign guilt for the past. We come to forge a partnership with the present to repair the future.” He said the ultimate goal was to ensure that Africa’s cultural heritage continued through its return to the communities and institutions from which it was taken.

items.title: Purported kidnap of Adeleke’s aide plot to blackmail APC, Tinubu – Osun APC
items.description: By Shina Abubakar The All Progressives Congress APC in Osun State has berated Governor Ademola Adeleke-led administration over attempt to heat up the polity with fake kidnap of an aide of the governor, Shakiru Babatunde and blame on its on the party. The APC, in a statement issued by its Director of Media and Information Kola Olabisi on Wednesday, urged the police not to succumb to pressure from government officials to bury the matter, saying the arrested suspect must face the law. “We gathered that the intention of the kidnap conspirators was to demonize the Osun State APC and incite the public against them as well and criminalise the Federal Government of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu as a failed administration under whose nose criminality has festered. “The obnoxious intention is to undermine the chances of President Tinubu to earn a re-election in January 2027. “It is a criminal offence for anyone to fake his or her kidnapping. The offender upon conviction is liable to 10-20 years imprisonment. It is unfortunate that this is a grave offence some officials of the state government in collusion with pliable security agents want to sweep under the carpet. “We are appealing to the state Commissioner of Police in the state, CP Ibrahim D. Zungura, to pay a particular attention to this case to serve as a deterrent to future criminal act”, the party added. However Governor Adeleke’s spokesperson Olawale Rasheed in a statement debunked claims that government officials are trying to sweep the matter under the carpet, saying government is supporting police investigation. He added that government reported the said kidnap to the police at first instance, hence, there is no reason to block or prevent investigation in the matter. “We categorically denied the fake news that there were attempts by the state officials to bribe the police to sweep the matter under the carpet. Such reports are unfounded and baseless conjectures. “Nobody in the government is attempting to bribe the police and the police have not received any kobo from state officials as libelously asserted in a publication. “The police are currently investigating the matter while the state government is also waiting for the outcome of the investigation for further action. “We therefore call on members of the public to ignore any misinformation designed to tarnish the image of state officials or the police as relevant police units are currently investigating the entire episode”, he added. items.title: The Makings of a Prewar World
items.description: Donald Trump offered perhaps the clearest summation yet of his worldview in an otherwise discursive address to the United Nations General Assembly yesterday. Defending the American takeover of Venezuelan oil, he invoked an old maxim: “To the victor belongs the spoils.” He then presented Iran with a choice between accepting his terms and being driven “into hell with no chance of survival.” These remarks are the latest sign that world politics is entering an era when might makes right. Yet Trump is only one of the leaders driving this rupture from the post–World War II international order. Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping have also broken the order, although their methods differ profoundly—morally, legally, and otherwise. American policy may change when Trump leaves office in January 2029, but Putin and Xi may remain in power well into the next decade. A new American president will likely not be able to restore the old order or create a better one, even if they want to. Their greatest challenge will be to arrest the slide. International order is a notoriously vague and politically contested concept. Many leaders in the global South, along with Western critics, reject the idea that the United States ever consistently abided by a rules-based system. They point to Western military interventions, double standards, and the unequal distribution of power within international institutions. But the old order’s failures do not mean that its restraints were meaningless. In his first book, A World Restored , Henry Kissinger argued that a stable and legitimate order rests on a limited consensus: an understanding among the major powers about what he called the permissible aims and methods of foreign policy. Governments can compete intensely and violate rules without seeking to overturn the system itself. The danger arises when a major power becomes so dissatisfied with the limits imposed upon it that it adopts a revolutionary foreign policy. [ Vivian Salama: America’s allies are no longer waiting for Trump to leave ] Under the old international order, major powers did not, as a general rule, conquer and annex the territory of their neighbors. The global trading system was based on reciprocity, tariffs were historically low, and markets were relatively open. And, although it was the world’s strongest country, the United States exercised enough self-discipline to allow its allies to grow into genuine partners, not vassals to be constantly squeezed for concessions. Over the past decade, and decisively since the pandemic, that consensus about permissible conduct has collapsed. Putin launched the largest war in Europe since World War II with his invasion of Ukraine in 2022. He more than anyone has revived the idea that countries can expand their borders through the use of force. Combined Russian- and Ukrainian-military casualties (those killed, wounded, and missing) have reached approximately 2 million people. European governments have accused Russia of an expanding campaign of sabotage, cyberattacks, arson, and drone incursions below the threshold of conventional war. North Korea has intervened directly in this war, and many other nations are indirectly involved—China and Iran on the side of Russia; Europe, the United States (at least under Joe Biden), and Asian democracies on the side of Ukraine. Under Xi, China has broken the global trading system. Xi has used the power of the Chinese state to establish dominance in advanced manufacturing, reduce China’s imports as much as possible, and aggressively grow its exports. The result is that China has enormous excess capacity. Its goods flood into the rest of the world at prices impossible to compete with, leaving other countries to choose between deindustrialization and protectionism. More and more of them are selecting the latter. This policy is not as morally egregious as Putin’s invasion of Ukraine, but it has toppled a key pillar of the international economic order. Since taking office for a second term, in 2025, Trump has turned American power against U.S. allies and partners. He imposed the highest tariffs in nearly a century on Canada, Japan, South Korea, India, and the European Union and used the threat of more to extract hundreds of billions of dollars in investment pledges. He mused about making Canada the 51st state and seizing Greenland. He pushed Ukraine to sign over a share of its mineral wealth in the middle of a war for its national survival. Under Trump, the United States sees itself not as the guarantor of an alliance system of like-minded democracies, but as a dominant power that wields its influence for singular, transactional gain. Trump has broken the restraint that made American primacy tolerable to most of the rest of the world. Reports suggest that he may meet Xi and Putin for a “big three” trilateral on the margins of the Asia Pacific Economic Summit in Shenzhen in November, which could mark the formal end of the old order. The rupture has produced an international environment that feels ever more like that of a prewar period. This does not mean that a major conflict is inevitable. But if one occurs, future historians will not find its causes sudden or mysterious. They are in plain sight. [ Listen: Trump battles against an economy of his making ] The major powers are building up their militaries and racing to master drone warfare and artificial intelligence. Trump’s lack of commitment to alliances, especially in Europe, raises the prospect that an aggressor may calculate that it can act without triggering much of a U.S. reaction. Meanwhile, America’s rivals are more and more aligned as they integrate their military production, share sensitive technology, and assist one another in battle. The shift has generational and psychological drivers. Putin, Xi, and Trump are elderly, sometimes erratic, insulated in information bubbles, and animated by ideological visions of national revival. The moment may feel like a closing window—a now-or-never opportunity to remake the world while they still can. A future American president may promise to build a new and improved international order. But Xi and Putin will have little reason to accept the restraints that Washington wants to restore, and although American allies may welcome a return to a more internationalist U.S. foreign policy, they will harbor doubts that it will survive the next election. Rather than promising what they cannot deliver, aspiring presidents should level with the American people. The international order has come to an end. The next president will inherit one of the most unforgiving international environments since 1945. Their task will be to stop the deterioration, inject some stability into world affairs, and begin to lay the foundation for a better future, even if that is not achievable in the short term.

items.title: EFCC declares ex-pension boss Abdulrasheed Maina wanted over alleged stolen property
items.description: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has declared Abdulrasheed Maina, former chairman of the defunct Pension Reform Task Team (PRTT), wanted over an alleged case of receiving stolen property. This was revealed in a tweet on Wednesday by the anti-graft agency. In the notice, the EFCC described Maina as an indigene of Biu, Borno State, and appealed to members of the public with information about his whereabouts to contact the commission. “Anybody with useful information as to his whereabouts should please contact the Commission in its Ibadan, Uyo, Sokoto, Maiduguri, Benin, Makurdi, Kaduna, Ilorin, Enugu, Kano, Lagos, Gombe, Port Harcourt or Abuja offices or through 08093322644; its e-mail address: info@efcc.gov.ng or the nearest Police Station and other security agencies.” ABDULRASHEED ABDULLAHI MAINA IS WANTED BY THE EFCC pic.twitter.com/Eap2k9SIS5 — EFCC Nigeria (@officialEFCC) September 23, 2026 The latest declaration is not the first time the EFCC has declared Maina wanted. In 2015, the commission declared him wanted over his alleged involvement in a pension biometric contracts case involving former Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, Steve Oronsaye, and two others. The EFCC had said Maina was charged alongside Oronsaye and others before the Federal High Court in Abuja on a 24-count charge bordering on procurement fraud and obtaining by false pretence. Maina also faced prosecution by the commission in 2019 over allegations of pension fraud and money laundering. items.title: Préparation de la rentrée scolaire : un Conseil interministériel prévu vendredi
items.description: Le Premier ministre Ahmadou Al Aminou Lô présidera, vendredi 25 septembre 2026 à 9h30, un Conseil interministériel consacré à la préparation de la rentrée scolaire 2026-2027. La rencontre se tiendra à la salle de réunion n°1 du 10e étage du Building administratif Président Mamadou Dia. Cette réunion intervient alors que le calendrier officiel de l’année scolaire 2026-2027 a déjà été fixé par arrêté du ministère de l’Éducation nationale. Elle doit permettre au Gouvernement de faire le point sur les conditions matérielles, pédagogiques et administratives nécessaires au démarrage de l’année scolaire. Les précédentes réunions consacrées à la rentrée ont notamment porté sur l’état des infrastructures, les effectifs et les besoins en personnel, l’accès à l’eau et à l’électricité, les équipements scolaires, ainsi que la gestion des établissements exposés aux effets de l’hivernage. En septembre 2024, le Gouvernement avait ainsi arrêté une série de mesures concernant notamment les abris provisoires, les salles de classe, les tables-bancs et l’amélioration de l’environnement scolaire. Pour la rentrée 2026-2027, les autorités devront également tenir compte des difficultés encore signalées dans certaines zones, notamment en matière d’infrastructures et de mobilier scolaire. Le SAEMSS a récemment alerté sur le déficit de tables-bancs et la persistance des abris provisoires. Cette rencontre devrait ainsi permettre d’arrêter les dernières dispositions pour assurer un démarrage effectif et ordonné de l’année scolaire. C.G.D

items.title: A Revealing Exchange Between Donald Trump and Kaitlan Collins
items.description: When CNN’s Kaitlan Collins approached President Trump with a question about the Iran war at the United Nations General Assembly yesterday, the president scolded her for being there at all. “I’m surprised that CNN is here covering me,” Trump said, adding, “You should not be here covering me.” Presumably, he said this because CNN is among the three outlets , along with MS NOW and Politico , that Trump has barred from White House grounds because he didn’t like their coverage. But, to state the obvious, the United Nations is not the White House. If a journalist is denied a press pass from one entity, she’s not precluded from getting credentialed by another. As Collins said to Trump, “The United Nations allowed us in, sir.” The exchange highlights Trump’s warped understanding of journalism—in which stories are either good or bad, reporters are “ friendly ” or “ terrible ,” and a president decides who covers him and who doesn’t. “There’s something wrong with a country that can allow people to write purposely negative stories,” he said when he banned CNN and the other two outlets. “Now, if they want to write them, that’s fine. But I don’t have to let them into my—into the people’s house.” As Trump noted when he corrected himself, the White House serves the American people—but so does the press. Since the days of FDR, a cadre of rotating print, TV, and radio reporters have traveled with the president wherever he goes, including on weekends and holidays, to provide an unbroken and independent record of everything the president says and does in public. This press pool exists because not every reporter can constantly trail the president; neither can every citizen. Political reporters stand in for people who want to know what their most important elected representative is doing, but who have day jobs. [ Read: President Piggy ] The importance of the pool became especially visible this week when, in solidarity, the other four networks that typically share pool duties with CNN—ABC, CBS, Fox News, and NBC— suspended their pool coverage of the president. This led to an unintentionally Veep -like moment during Trump’s unveiling of his new helipad, when no networks provided audio as Trump appeared flanked by smiling construction workers, speaking without sound. (A Newsmax host gingerly described the scene as a sign that the CNN ban was perhaps “backfiring just a little bit.”) Trump has a long history with the press—and of seeming not to understand how it works. (As with many things pertaining to the president, however, determining whether his ignorance is genuine or strategic can be difficult.) At times, he has appeared to feign confusion in an effort to get reporters to do what he wants. In a 1997 New Yorker profile , for instance, Trump repeatedly told the reporter following him that his words were “off the record, but you can use it”—guidance that makes no sense, because “off the record” is an agreement that means a reporter can’t use a piece of information in a story. When he was campaigning for president in 2016, Trump frequently railed against “libel laws” and promised to “loosen them up” but struggled to describe what that meant. (“I’d have to get my lawyers in to tell you,” he told The Washington Post .) He suggested that late-night comedians should devote “equal time” to jokes about Democrats and his administration, seemingly invoking a law that doesn’t apply to either presidents or late-night jokes. [ Read: The press is not the root of Trump’s problems ] A fact that seems to bedevil Trump most is that the press doesn’t take orders from him, and that therefore almost every reporter he encounters will at some point seem “unfriendly.” In his current term, one of Trump’s first orders of business was to decree that the White House would choose the reporters in the press pool, breaking with the tradition of news organizations choosing. He’s trying to ban the Associated Press from parts of the White House because the wire service continues to refer, against Trump’s wishes, to the body of water south of the United States as “the Gulf of Mexico.” Trump regularly interrogates pool reporters about which network they’re really with, and dubs the answer “fake news” if it’s not one that he likes. As evidenced by the exchange at the United Nations, CNN’s Collins seems to provoke his disdain to an unusual degree: Over the years, Trump has attempted to bar her from White House press events, tried to make her sit in the back of the press room, called her “ stupid ” and “ nasty ,” implored her to smile , and told her she should be ashamed of herself because she used to be “a conservative from Alabama.” To which Collins replied, “I’m still from Alabama, sir.” Presidents have always had testy relations with the press, of course, and have tried to minimize negative coverage. The behavior of Trump’s administration, however, often shades into something more sinister. His FBI raided the home of a Washington Post reporter whose coverage he found objectionable, and Trump has sued and defunded news organizations whose coverage he deemed biased. MS NOW reported in May that the FBI had opened a criminal investigation focusing on my colleague Sarah Fitzpatrick, related to an article she wrote about FBI Director Kash Patel. (The FBI has denied the existence of such an investigation.) As a reporter, I spend a lot of time explaining to sources—many of whom have never interacted with the media—the basics of journalism: that we don’t accept or grant payment for interviews, that reporters don’t interact with advertisers, and that most mainstream outlets pride themselves on not affiliating with any given political ideology. Some degree of media illiteracy is understandable at a time when thousands of local newspapers have closed , and when influencers—some of whom secretly accept payment for their branded videos—compete for attention on social media with journalists reporting the truth. Journalists shouldn’t have to explain their jobs, though, to someone who has lived his entire adult life in the public eye, and who is now America’s most important public servant. But as Collins showed at the UN, apparently, they must.
